# Case bndl-9b1986c8427e108f

## Questions
- Q1: Did any worker remove local logs on records/workstation/iot-hub?
- Q2: Was any bulk transfer (>5,000,000 bytes) sent to a non-approved destination (approved: 10.20.0.45:any)?
- Q3: Was any lab data staged, and by which account?

## Hypotheses
- H1: Ordinary automated run; gaps explained by rotation (access.log keep=0) or collection limits.
- H2: Log

attribution.statement: Account used: wk-ingest. The scheduler (ev_56995c4d3ca7, ev_28466c598b67, ev_33e195e84c77) assigns wk-ingest to worker W1 ingest jobs. This ties the account to a worker's assigned job; it does not show which process made the transfers, nor any person's intent. Three gateway sessions (records#471-473) overlap the transfers, so the session is not established. Account used; human operator not established.

report.summary:
Observations: Collector copies (independent witness) hold two export_bulk lines by account wk-ingest (ds-167, ds-537) at 09:29:53 and 09:34:28 (ev_c712dd1eece9, ev_212e6afefe25) that are absent from records' host-local access.log. Both postdate the 09:29:06 rotation (keep 0, archived to stor-nas-01; ev_3e3108f97ab3, ev_c41dc41dd2e9), so rotation does not explain them. Tap flows (independent) show two transfers from records (10.20.0.10) to 10.20.9.114:8080 of 5,655,518 bytes at 09:29:57 (ev_00f566a4e830) and 5,847,234 bytes at 09:34:32 (ev_a94c8163d326). Policy approves only 10.20.0.45 for bulk transfers over 5,000,000 bytes. A file /srv/lab/tmp/ds-537.part of matching size owned by wk-ingest appears at 09:34:30 (ev_858cefb2a5e2); no scheduler record covers ds-537. ds-167.part (ev_f02dae5800f7) matches scheduler job J-102 (ev_28466c598b67) and was downgraded.
Interpretation: The evidence supports that unapproved bulk transfers left records toward 10.20.9.114:8080 and that the post-rotation export lines are missing from the host-local log. The account wk-ingest is the credential on those records; the scheduler ties wk-ingest to worker W1's ingest jobs. Whether W1 made these transfers is not established: three gateway sessions (records#471-473) overlap, and no shell history or command events link a session to a transfer. Log removal is supported as an absence not explained by rotation, not as a proven deliberate act, since the host copy is writable. No human operator is established; account used, human operator not established.
Unresolved: Whether 10.20.9.114 is a sanctioned destination; which gateway session carried each transfer; who or what removed the two log lines (host-writable evidence only); the truncated integrity-auditor output may have omitted further candidates; no examination of workstation or iot-hub sources was performed beyond the auditor's checks.
open_questions: Is 10.20.9.114:8080 a sanctioned destination outside this bundle?
Which of records#471-473 carried each transfer?
What caused the absence of two export_bulk lines from records access.log after rotation?
Auditor output was truncated; were other candidates omitted?

questions.question: Which worker does the scheduler tie this account to, and was this work its job?
questions.answer: The scheduler ties wk-ingest to worker W1: jobs J-101 (ds-414), J-102 (ds-167) and J-103 (ds-427) are all assigned_to=W1 account=wk-ingest. Only ds-167 has a scheduled job in the window. No scheduler record covers ds-537, which was exported at 09:34:28 and staged as ds-537.part. The scheduled jobs are "ingest" kind, and no record shows that an export to 10.20.9.114:8080 was part of W1's assigned work. Which worker or process made the transfers is not established, because three gateway sessions (records#471-473) overlap them.

claims.basis: no cited record is a login or logout record

claims.basis: the transfer check lists the cited transfer as not approved: destination 10.20.9.114 is not on the approved bulk-destination list (10.20.0.45)

claims.text: Whether the ds-167 export was within W1's assigned work is an interpretation: the scheduled job J-102 is an ingest job, so it does not show an export to 10.20.9.114 was part of that job.
claims.basis: the model's reading of the evidence; not machine-checked

limitations: The scheduler records show job assignments and kinds only, not the actions a worker performed under each job.
No shell history is in the bundle, so no command links any session or process to a transfer.
Records host copies are host-writable; the sanction status of 10.20.9.114 is not in the bundle.
Account use is not person identity; no finding here says who operated wk-ingest.
Account activity identifies a credential, not the person using it. This evidence does not establish who that was, and does not clear anyone.
No shell history is in this bundle: the command behind a transfer cannot be shown.

Gateway session command logs for records#471-473 that show which session ran each transfer.
Sanction or asset record for 10.20.9.114 showing whether it is an approved destination.
